data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=matlab-svd
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks=1
#   --cpus-per-task=1
#   --mem-per-cpu=4G
#   --time=00:02:00
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   --reservation=gpuprimer

#flux: --job-name=matlab-svd
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=2m

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu=4G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --reservation=gpuprimer
# Flux reservation selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may not run on the reserved resources, increasing queue time or preventing workshop-specific access.

module purge
module load matlab/R2019a

matlab -singleCompThread -nodisplay -nosplash -r svd_matlab

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this can allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run slower.
The original Slurm job requested memory per CPU (`--mem-per-cpu=4G`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job.

The original Slurm job used a reservation (`--reservation=gpuprimer`) but the Flux resource section has no reservation selection; this may prevent use of the intended reserved resources and change scheduling/eligibility.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=matlab-svd    # create a short name for your job
#SBATCH --nodes=1                # node count
#SBATCH --ntasks=1               # total number of tasks across all nodes
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1        # cpu-cores per task (>1 if multi-threaded tasks)
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=4G         # memory per cpu-core (4G is default)
#SBATCH --time=00:02:00          # total run time limit (HH:MM:SS)
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1             # number of gpus per node
#SBATCH --reservation=gpuprimer  # REMOVE THIS LINE AFTER THE WORKSHOP

module purge
module load matlab/R2019a

matlab -singleCompThread -nodisplay -nosplash -r svd_matlab
